Aggregate estimates across treatment groups

Source: R/aggregate_estimands.R
aggregate_estimands.Rd

Averages the treatment-group-specific estimates from multiple_treatment_group_analysis across treatment groups, by event time (Leventer 2025, Section 5). The default weights are the treatment-group shares in the sample. Standard errors account for persons who serve as controls for several treatment groups.

Usage

aggregate_estimands(
  results,
  weights = "sample",
  methods = c("DID_Female", "DID_Male", "TD", "Conventional", "NTD", "TD_E_LOGS",
    "TD_PR"),
  include_pre = FALSE
)

Arguments

results

The data.frame returned by multiple_treatment_group_analysis, unmodified (its attributes carry the influence functions). A table without them is accepted, with standard errors under an independence approximation and a warning.

weights

How to weight treatment groups:

  • "sample" (default): treatment-group shares. Within gender, \(w_{g,d} = n_{g,d} / \sum_{k} n_{g,k}\), for DID_Female and DID_Male; across genders, \(w_d = n_d / \sum_{k} n_{k}\), for all other methods.

  • "uniform" or NULL: equal weight per treatment group.

  • A named numeric vector (names = treatment groups): fixed weights, renormalized to sum to one over the groups present at each event time. Groups missing from the vector get weight zero, with a warning.

methods

Methods to aggregate (default: all). DID_Female, DID_Male: weighted_avg and ratio_of_avgs of theta; Conventional: weighted_avg of gap_theta; NTD and TD_E_LOGS: weighted_avg of rho_effect and of the accounting rows rho_obs, rho_cf, share_parenthood, share_other; TD: weighted_avg of gap_ATE; TD_PR: weighted_avg of gap_theta_pre.

include_pre

Logical (default FALSE). Also aggregate pre-treatment event times. A pre-treatment event time has one cell per control group (control_offset = \(d' - d\)), and each offset is aggregated separately, so each row is the validation test of one treatment-control distance.

Value

A data.frame with one row per event time, estimand, method and aggregation type: event_time, control_offset (\(d' - d\); after treatment it is event_time + 1), estimand, method, agg_type, est, se, n_groups (treatment groups with positive weight), ci_l, ci_h (est -/+ 1.96 se), t, p.

Details

agg_type = "weighted_avg" is \(\sum_d w_d B_d\) over the treatment-group estimates \(B_d\). For DID_Female / DID_Male this is \(\theta_{Agg,1}(g, e)\); for Conventional it is the conventional aggregate gap \(\Delta\theta_{Agg}(e)\), which under NTD is biased for the gap in normalized effects (Theorem 1); for NTD it is \(\rho_{Agg}(e)\), the aggregate effect of parenthood on the gender earnings ratio. agg_type = "ratio_of_avgs" (DID rows only) is \(\theta_{Agg,2}(g, e)\), the ratio of the weighted average ATE to the weighted average APO; it puts more weight on higher-earning groups, which is why the paper prefers \(\theta_{Agg,1}\) (Section 5.1).

Standard errors. The influence function of an aggregate (aggregate estimator section of the appendix on estimation and inference) sums the treatment-group influence functions with the weights; with weights = "sample" it adds the term for the estimated shares, \(\psi_{A(e)} = P_e^{-1}\sum_d [(B_d - A(e))\psi_{p_d} + p_d\psi_{B_d}]\), \(\psi_{p_d} = 1\{D = d\} - p_d\), where \(p_d\) is the share of persons in group \(d\) (\(1\{G = g, D = d\} - p_{g,d}\) with the joint share of gender \(g\) and group \(d\) for the within-gender DID rows) and \(P_e\) the summed share of the aggregated groups. For ratio_of_avgs the chain rule is applied to the ratio of the two weighted averages, each with its share term. Standard errors are clustered by person. The share term is put on the person-age scale with the average number of ages per person, exact for a balanced panel.

Not every treatment group has an estimate at every event time; each event time uses the groups present, and n_groups reports how many.

See also

multiple_treatment_group_analysis, bias_bounds

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- simulate_data(n_individuals = 2000)
res <- multiple_treatment_group_analysis(sim, treatment_groups = 24:26,
  periods_post = 2, periods_pre = NULL, verbose = FALSE)
#> 1 cells could not be estimated (see attr(result, "skipped")), e.g.: No women with age at first birth 26 observed at age 28.
agg <- aggregate_estimands(res)
agg[agg$method %in% c("NTD", "Conventional"), ]
